subject: 3code
title: dmail: the model reverts its own conversation to a [checkpoint N] marker mid-turn and carries a self-addressed note forward; filesystem deliberately NOT reverted
evidence: src/threecode/prompts.nim:2983-2987 (tool schema), prompts.nim:2629 (usage rules), src/threecode/session.nim:705,923,1201 (dispatcher + wire record), tests/core/test_dmail.nim (26 tests)
one_why: Every other checkpoint-revert in the corpus is user- or harness-side; this inverts authority so the agent does its own context surgery when a huge read or failed debug bloats the window, with the filesystem kept as the durable ground truth - economy executed by the model instead of paid for by the harness.

subject: 3code
title: Zero-token flailing detector: call fingerprints over a bounded window with four signals (identical-consecutive, spaced A-B-A-B, no-progress repeats, Jaccard near-duplicate streak clustering), escalating SYSTEM notes x3 then turn abort, every intervention visible in scrollback
evidence: src/threecode/turns.nim:16-60 (thresholds + signal design), turns.nim:652 (detector in loop), docs/manual.md:634-648, tests/core/test_flail.nim (26 tests), tests/flail_replay.nim
one_why: Detection spends no model tokens and no judge model; the near-duplicate clustering (avg pairwise Jaccard over a ring, FlailStreakJaccard/NearDup/Cluster) catches paraphrased thrash that exact-fingerprint detectors miss, while successful idempotent polls are explicitly exempted from false flags.

subject: 3code
title: Default-on kernel fence with zero approval prompts: Landlock/Seatbelt/restricted-token FS policy on every tool call, dual enforcement (in-process checks reload policy on mtime before each restricted op AND the bash subprocess re-loads the policy file itself), hidden guard rules no policy file can weaken, host rules routed through a CONNECT+SOCKS5 egress allowlist proxy
evidence: src/threecode/sandbox.nim:26-31 (hidden rules), :36-40 (dual reload), :64-82 (default policy), :489 (Landlock/Seatbelt lowering), box.nim:9,35,63, wall.nim:8-14 (proxy), tests/core/test_sandbox_cascade.nim, test_sandbox_traversal.nim, test_wall_bash.nim
one_why: Nuance vs octomind: 3code deletes the approval layer entirely and argues it in writing - 'approval prompts are security by interruption ... train users to mash yes' (docs/manual.md ~1247-1260) - with the honest calibration that most rival sessions run unfenced anyway; the shipped default still leaves network wide open (allow *) and the enforcement engine lives in the author's external sandwall library.

subject: 3code
title: Three context tiers with the model holding two: dmail checkpoint fold, then the clear tool ending a chunk with written handoff instructions for the next session (chunked/cybernetic modes over plan files + worktrees), auto-summarize kept as the last-resort fallback at 0.8 window, keep-8, at-most-once-per-turn
evidence: src/threecode/compact.nim:1-6,53-59, src/threecode/actions.nim:106,125 (clear tool), docs/manual.md:886-949 (chunked + cybernetic), src/threecode/skills/cybernetic-plan.md, docs/cache-analysis.md:14 (95.67% cache hit vs rivals)
one_why: The ladder prefers discarding spent context over repeatedly re-summarizing it - 'this loses less information than repeatedly summarizing all the old work' - and the published per-task cost table shows the bet measured against five rival harnesses on the same model.

subject: 3code
title: Byte-reproducible agent binary as a CI gate: container pinned by sha256 digest, apt frozen to a snapshot.ubuntu.com timestamp, sha256-pinned Nim toolchain, clean-rebuild byte-equality check, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH double-pack check with perturbed mtimes
evidence: .github/workflows/linux-amd64.yml:17-135 (image digest, snapshot sed, NIM_SHA256, 'Reproducibility check (rebuild from scratch)', pack-twice hash compare), tests/test_build_provenance.nim
one_why: No other reviewed subject makes the shipped binary verifiably rebuildable; for a tool that runs on your box with your API keys, supply-chain trust becomes checkable rather than assumed - and the workflow comments document exactly why each freeze exists.

subject: 3code
title: Self-built cross-platform PTY expect harness in Nim: one TtySession API over openpty (POSIX) and ConPTY (Windows kernel32 declarations hand-rolled), driving the real binary through a ttty grid with frame-snapshot artifacts on failure - 53 functional tty specs
evidence: tests/tty_expect.nim:1-9 (openpty/ConPTY), :36-46 (winlean CreatePseudoConsole declarations), tests/tty/test_tty_functional.nim (3,885 LOC, 53 tests), .github/workflows/linux-amd64.yml test job (runner kernel PTY/landlock access note)
one_why: The scrollback-purity design ('every rendering bug 3code ever had lived in the footer') is defended end-to-end: exit codes, cursor placement, bar repaints and submit-eating bugs are tested against the actual terminal, not a simulated renderer - the harness itself is the scarce asset.

subject: 3code
title: Patient retry sized to outlive subscription caps: exponential backoff to a 2048s ceiling for ~36 hours on 429/5xx/network, retries after the initial window printed into the transcript as numbered rows, separate rate-vs-server backoff ledgers, Esc cancels
evidence: docs/manual.md:588-613 ('long enough to outwait a rolling limit'), src/threecode/api.nim:289-297 (429 classifier), api.nim:394-397 (split rate/server retry levels), tests/test_429_typing_during_backoff.nim
one_why: Purpose-built for the README's core promise - start a task on a 5-hour capped subscription, walk away, it resumes when the window resets; the split backoff ledgers stop a 5xx burst from inflating the budget a later 429 sees.

subject: 3code
title: Live token bar repainted with accurate post-call usage, then committed as a same-tone 'receipt' row in scrollback when the user submits the next turn - spend history becomes part of the transcript the user keeps
evidence: src/threecode/fatprompt/runtime.nim:63-79 (pendingHint lifecycle: live rough -> accurate -> receipt), docs/manual.md:479-587 (The screen)
one_why: Cost visibility with zero chrome: no status bar or TUI, just a per-turn receipt in the same scrollback the user greps - nuance vs codebuff's internal receipt accounting, which never surfaces to the user.

subject: 3code
title: Skills priced at zero when unused: system prompt carries only a one-bullet-per-skill catalog, the model reads a skill file with the normal read tool when the task smells like it, filename is the trigger, four-tier override dirs including the vendor-neutral .agents/skills/ - and an explicit anti-MCP rationale
evidence: src/threecode/prompts.nim:1145 ('do not preload the catalog'), src/threecode/skills/ (6 built-ins), docs/manual.md:906-931 (discovery order + 'deliberately no MCP-style plugin protocol')
one_why: Convergence data point for lazy skill loading, distinctive in stating the context-cost argument outright: 'a skill file plus command-line tools covers the same ground at a fraction of the context cost.'

subject: 3code
title: Sessions persist the verbatim wire bytes of every request (key order, extra fields, raw argument bytes) so a resumed session re-sends byte-identical history and the provider prompt cache stays hot; stable conversation-id header per session for provider-side cache/routing affinity
evidence: src/threecode/session.nim:645-655 (recordToToolCall prefers wire section), :890-893 ('prompt cache stays hot'), src/threecode/turns.nim:676-681 (conversation id recomputed per turn, shared across tool-call loop), docs/manual.md:1287-1289 ('byte-identically, so the prompt cache stays warm')
one_why: Cache discipline at the persistence layer rather than the request layer: most subjects rebuild history from parsed records and silently eat a full-price cache miss on every resume; the legacy-rebuild comment even documents which fields older logs lose.
